questions.stem: A 45-year-old male presents with epigastric pain and melena. Upper endoscopy reveals a well-defined ulcer with a punched-out appearance in the gastric antrum. Histological examination of the ulcer base shows inflammatory cells, granulation tissue, and fibrosis. What is the most likely histological finding from superficial to deep in this ulcer?

options.label: A
options.text: Inflammatory infiltrate---Necrotic debris----- Granulation tissue---Fibrous tissue

options.label: C
options.text: Necrotic debris----- Granulation tissue---Inflammatory infiltrate--- Fibrous tissue

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Necrotic debris-----Inflammatory infiltrate---Granulation tissue---Fibrous tissue

 

This is a classic description of the histological zones of a healing peptic ulcer or any chronic ulcer. From superficial to deep, the layers seen on histopathology are:

 

  • Necrotic debris – superficial layer of dead tissue and cellular debris.
  • Inflammatory infiltrate – primarily neutrophils in acute ulcers, mixed inflammation in chronic ones.
  • Granulation tissue – newly forming connective tissue and small blood vessels.
  • Fibrous tissue (scar) – dense collagen laid down during the healing process.

 

Mnemonic:

 

N-I-G-F → "Never Ignore Gastric Fibrosis"

 

  • N = Necrotic debris
  • I = Inflammatory cells
  • G = Granulation tissue
  • F = Fibrous scar tissue

 

Clinical Relevance:

 

  • These features are typically seen in chronic peptic ulcers, especially in the gastric antrum or duodenum.
  • Helps distinguish ulcers from malignancies (which may not show orderly healing zones).

questions.stem: A second-year medical student Ravi Kumar is reading the chapter of gastrointestinal tract from “Review of Pathology” book. To test his thoroughness of concepts, you ask him to consider the following statements regarding inflammatory bowel disease: Ulcerative colitis (UC) involves terminal ileum and rarely causes proctitis Cobblestone appearance of bowel is seen in Crohn's disease Skip lesions are a characteristic of ulcerative colitis but never seen in Crohn's disease Ulcerative colitis is more common in smokers than non-smokers Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
The following have strong causal association with H. pylori infection except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Gastric adenoma

 

  • H. pylori infection is not strongly associated with gastric adenomas, which are benign tumors of the gastric epithelium.
  • Gastric adenomas are more commonly associated with familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) or sporadic mutations rather than H. pylori infection. 

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Chronic gastritis: There is a strong causal association between H. pylori infection and chronic gastritis. H. pylori is a major cause of chronic active gastritis, characterized by inflammation of the gastric mucosa.

 

Option B. Peptic ulcer disease: H. pylori infection is strongly associated with the development of peptic ulcer disease, particularly duodenal ulcers. H. pylori colonization in the gastric mucosa can lead to mucosal damage and ulcer formation.

 

Option C. Gastric carcinoma: H. pylori infection is considered a major risk factor for the development of gastric carcinoma, particularly intestinal-type gastric adenocarcinoma. Chronic inflammation and mucosal damage induced by H. pylori contribute to the carcinogenic process.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Various gastrointestinal conditions strong causal association with H. pylori infection, including chronic gastritis, peptic ulcer disease, and gastric carcinoma, but Duodenal adenomas do not have a strong causal association with H. pylori infection.

 

Summary:

 

  • H. pylori → chronic gastritis → hyperplastic gastric polyps 
  • H. pylori → gastric adenomas/adenocarcinoma (via atrophic gastritis & intestinal metaplasia) 
  • H. pylori → duodenal ulcers 
  • H. pylori → gastricl adenomas (Not causally related)

 

H. pylori-Associated Infections and Tumors

 

Ref: Robbins 10th/ 774

questions.stem: A 32-year-old male presents with recurrent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. Colonoscopy reveals multiple aphthous ulcers, skip lesions, and areas of cobblestone appearance in the terminal ileum and colon. Biopsy of the affected mucosa demonstrates transmural inflammation with non-caseating granulomas. Which of the following histological findings is most characteristic of Crohn's disease in the biopsy of this patient?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C. Non-caseating granulomas

questions.stem: A 55-year-old male presents with longstanding gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) refractory to proton pump inhibitors. Upper endoscopy reveals a change in the distal esophageal mucosa characterized by salmon-colored, velvety epithelium extending several centimeters above the gastroesophageal junction. Biopsy of this tissue shows intestinal metaplasia with goblet cells. Which of the following complications is this patient at increased risk for?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A. Esophageal adenocarcinoma

questions.stem: A 35-year-old male presents to the gastroenterology clinic with a family history of colorectal cancer. His father was diagnosed with colorectal cancer at age 40, and his grandfather died of colorectal cancer at age 50. The patient is asymptomatic and has no significant medical history. On physical examination, there are no abnormal findings. Screening colonoscopy reveals the presence of numerous polyps throughout the colon, including the rectum. Biopsy of these polyps shows adenomatous changes. What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C. Familial Adenomatous Polyposis (FAP).

questions.stem: A 32-year-old traveler returning from a recent trip to a developing country presents with high fever, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. Physical examination reveals hepatosplenomegaly and abdominal tenderness. Gastrointestinal endoscopy reveals multiple discrete longitudinal ulcers with a raised, erythematous base in the distal ileum and colon. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C. Typhoid fever

questions.stemHtml: A 60-year-old man presents with a 5-week history of difficulty swallowing. Physical examination is unremarkable. Upper endoscopy shows a large mass in the upper third of the esophagus. A biopsy is shown in the image. Which of the following is the most important risk factor for development of the condition in the patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Cigarette smoking

 

Case details:

 

  • 60-year-old man
  • Progressive dysphagia (5 weeks) → suggests malignancy
  • Upper third of esophagus mass
  • Biopsy image shows squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of the esophagus.

 

Key point:

 

  • Upper and middle esophagus cancers -most commonly squamous cell carcinoma.
  • Distal esophagus cancers -most commonly adenocarcinoma (usually due to Barrett esophagus, GERD).

 

Major risk factors for esophageal SCC:

 

  • Most important (worldwide): Alcohol and smoking
  • Other risks: Plummer-Vinson syndrome, nitrosamines, hot beverages, caustic injury, achalasia.

 

Other Options: 

 

Option B. Exposure to aflatoxin: Hepatocellular carcinoma, not esophageal cancer.

 

Option C. Herpetic esophagitis: Causes ulcers, not SCC.


Option D. Reflux esophagitis: Linked to Barrett esophagus → adenocarcinoma of lower esophagus, not upper.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old female presents with chronic diarrhea, weight loss, and bloating. She reports that her symptoms worsen after consuming foods containing wheat, barley, or rye. A small bowel biopsy is performed, and histological examination reveals villous atrophy, increased intraepithelial lymphocytes, and crypt hyperplasia in the duodenal mucosa. Which of the following histological findings is most characteristic of celiac sprue?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A. Villous atrophy

questions.stemHtml: A 53-year-old woman complains of acute diarrhea and severe abdominal pain. She was recently treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics for community-acquired pneumonia. A CBC shows a WBC count of 24,000/μL. The patient subsequently develops septic shock and dies. A portion of her colon is shown at autopsy. These findings are typical of which of the following gastrointestinal diseases?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D. Pseudomembranous colitis

questions.stemHtml: A 45-year-old woman presents with sudden attacks of wheezing, shortness of breath, and episodic hot fl ashes. She also reports abdominal cramps and diarrhea. Physical examination shows facial redness, pitting edema of the lower legs, and a murmur of tricuspid regurgitation. A 24-hour urine specimen contains elevated levels of 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA). A CT scan of the abdomen demonstrates multiple 1 to 2-cm nodules in distal ileum. A small bowel resection is performed (shown in the image). The arrows point to submucosal tumors. Microscopic examination shows nests of cells with round and uniform nuclei. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C. Carcinoid tumor
